properties.name: Sized 2026-09-10: full-precision embeddings would MORE THAN DOUBLE the export; at 2 bits they are 7% of it
properties.statement:
RECORDED AS EVIDENCE ON AN OPEN QUESTION, NOT AS A PROPOSAL. It does not settle `dec:idea-embeddings-adoption` and it does not argue for adopting embeddings.

SOURCE: Anthony brought arXiv 2504.19874v1, "TurboQuant: Online Vector Quantization with Near-optimal Distortion Rate" (Zandieh, Daliri, Hadian, Mirrokni — Google Research / NYU / DeepMind), and asked whether anything in it was useful here. Its claim is a DATA-OBLIVIOUS quantizer — random rotation, then per-coordinate Lloyd-Max scalar quantizers whose codebooks are derived analytically from the resulting Beta distribution rather than fitted to any corpus — within a ~2.7 constant of the information-theoretic distortion bound at every bit-width.

MEASURED HERE, against this design's own numbers (4102 nodes, 15.07 MB export, dim 768 for nomic-embed-text-v1.5, which is the model the existing `embeddings-rs` sidecar serves; base64 inflation included because the export is JSON):

  float32   3072 B/node    16.80 MB    111.5% of the export
  8-bit      768 B/node     4.20 MB     27.9%
  4-bit      384 B/node     2.10 MB     13.9%
  2-bit      192 B/node     1.05 MB      7.0%
  1-bit       96 B/node     0.53 MB      3.5%

Paper's reported distortion on unit vectors: MSE ~0.117 and inner-product error ~0.56/d at 2 bits; ~0.03 and ~0.18/d at 3.

⭐ WHY THE TOP ROW MATTERS MORE THAN THE REST. Carrying full-precision vectors in the record is not a trade-off, it is off the table — the embeddings would be larger than the entire design. That is presumably why nobody has ever proposed it, and it is why the question "could the vectors live IN the export?" has not been asked. At 2 bits it becomes an ordinary question with an ordinary cost.

⚠️ WHAT THIS DOES NOT TOUCH, and it is the strongest leg of the case-against: THE MODEL DEPENDENCY. Quantization compresses vectors somebody else produced. It says nothing about whether reflow2 may depend on an embedding model, nothing about `req:thin-install`, and nothing about the one-binary posture. Point 5's per-path distinction and the sidecar-versus-provider argument in point 1 are untouched.

⚠️ AND IT IS NOT THE ANSWER TO THIS WEEK'S RETRIEVAL FAILURE. `fact:a-settled-question-was-re-asked-because-the-requirements-prose-outlived-its-decision` was a search miss, but of a specific kind: BM25 did not surface the Decision that GOVERNS the node being read, because that Decision is ABOUT A DIFFERENT SUBJECT than the query. Semantic similarity would likely have missed it for the same reason — the relation was structural, not lexical or semantic, and the edge was already in the graph. The fix for that was reading the edge. Nothing in this paper would have helped, and treating it as retrieval evidence would be reading the wrong lesson from a real incident.

CONFIDENCE 0.8 on the sizing, which is arithmetic; the distortion figures are the paper's own and have not been reproduced here.
